title: Key Concepts in Maritime Insurance
description: Test your understanding of the fundamental principles used in maritime insurance, including insurable interest, utmost good faith, indemnity, proximate cause, warranties, subrogation and contribution.

questions.question: What does insurable interest mean in maritime insurance?
options: The insured must have a genuine financial interest in the vessel, cargo or other insured subject
The insurer must own part of the insured vessel
The insured must purchase more than one insurance policy
The vessel must operate in international waters
questions.explanation: Insurable interest exists when a person or company would suffer a genuine financial loss if the insured vessel, cargo, freight or liability were damaged or lost.

questions.question: Which principle requires the insured to disclose important information honestly to the insurer?
options: Contribution
Utmost good faith
Subrogation
Indemnity
questions.explanation: Utmost good faith requires the parties to disclose material facts that could influence the insurer's assessment of the risk.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the principle of indemnity?
options: To guarantee that every claim is paid in full
To compensate the insured for the actual financial loss
To allow the insured to recover from several insurers
To transfer ownership of damaged property to the insurer
questions.explanation: Indemnity aims to restore the insured to approximately the same financial position as before the loss, subject to policy limits and deductibles.

questions.question: What does the principle of subrogation allow an insurer to do?
options: Increase the insured value after a casualty
Recover claim payments from a responsible third party
Require another insurer to pay the entire claim
Cancel a policy before its expiry date
questions.explanation: After paying a covered claim, the insurer may step into the insured's legal position and pursue a third party responsible for the loss.

questions.question: When does the principle of contribution normally apply?
options: When two or more insurers cover the same interest against the same risk
When the insured pays the premium in several instalments
When a claim involves both cargo and hull damage
When a shipowner contributes to a general average fund
questions.explanation: Contribution applies when the same interest is covered by multiple insurers, allowing them to share the loss proportionately.

questions.question: Which of the following is most likely to be considered a material fact when arranging hull insurance?
options: The agreed deductible under the proposed policy
The vessel's previous machinery failures and claims history
The insurer's internal administrative costs
The premium quoted by another insurer
questions.explanation: Previous machinery failures and claims can affect the insurer's decision to accept the risk, impose conditions or calculate the premium.

questions.question: What does proximate cause identify in a marine insurance claim?
options: The event that occurred first chronologically
The event physically closest to the damaged property
The dominant and effective cause of the loss
The party that first reported the casualty
questions.explanation: Proximate cause is the dominant and effective cause of the loss, not necessarily the first event or the event nearest in time.

questions.question: Which of the following is the best example of a marine insurance warranty?
options: A statement estimating the vessel's future market value
A condition requiring the vessel to remain within specified trading limits
A clause describing how the insurer calculates administrative fees
A recommendation that the master avoids severe weather
questions.explanation: Trading limits may be included as an express warranty or policy condition that the insured is required to comply with.

questions.question: Why does contribution prevent the insured from receiving more than the actual loss?
options: It allows the first insurer contacted to cancel the other policies
It limits the insured to recovering only the lowest policy limit
It requires insurers covering the same risk to share the claim proportionately
It transfers the insured's claim rights to the vessel owner
questions.explanation: Contribution divides the loss among insurers and prevents the insured from recovering the full claim separately under several policies.

questions.question: How do deductibles affect compensation under the principle of indemnity?
options: The deductible is added to the amount of the insured loss
The insurer compensates the actual covered loss after applying the deductible
The deductible only applies when another insurer is involved
The deductible determines whether the insured has insurable interest
questions.explanation: Indemnity is still subject to the terms of the policy, including deductibles, insured values, exclusions and limits.

questions.question: A cargo owner purchases insurance after transferring all ownership and financial risk in the goods to the buyer. The cargo owner would suffer no loss if the goods were damaged. Which principle is primarily affected?
options: Contribution
Insurable interest
Proximate cause
Subrogation
questions.explanation: A party that would not suffer a financial loss may no longer have the necessary insurable interest in the cargo.

questions.question: A shipowner fails to disclose that the vessel has experienced repeated main-engine breakdowns during the previous year. The information would have affected the insurer's underwriting decision. Which principle is most directly involved?
options: Utmost good faith
Contribution
Indemnity
Subrogation
questions.explanation: Repeated engine failures are material to the risk. Failure to disclose them may breach the duty of utmost good faith.

questions.question: A vessel encounters heavy weather. Poorly maintained hatch covers allow seawater to enter the cargo holds, damaging the cargo. Which principle is used to determine whether heavy weather or defective hatch covers were the legally effective cause of the loss?
options: Insurable interest
Contribution
Proximate cause
Subrogation
questions.explanation: Proximate cause analysis identifies the dominant and effective cause when several events or conditions contribute to a casualty.

questions.question: A cargo insurer pays a claim after cargo is damaged by a terminal operator's negligent handling. What may the insurer do next?
options: Use contribution to recover from the vessel's hull insurer
Use subrogation to pursue the negligent terminal operator
Use indemnity to increase the insured value of the cargo
Use proximate cause to transfer the policy to the terminal operator
questions.explanation: Subrogation allows the cargo insurer to pursue the negligent terminal operator after compensating the insured cargo owner.

questions.question: The same cargo interest is fully insured under two policies covering the same voyage and the same maritime risks. A covered loss occurs. How should the insurers normally respond?
options: Each insurer should pay the full loss independently
The insured should select one policy and permanently cancel the other
The insurers should share the loss according to the principle of contribution
Only the policy issued first should respond
questions.explanation: Contribution permits insurers covering the same interest and risk to divide the claim so that the insured does not recover more than the actual loss.

questions.question: A policy contains a condition that the vessel must not trade north of a specified latitude during winter. The vessel enters the restricted area and suffers damage. Which policy concept is most directly relevant?
options: A trading warranty
The principle of contribution
A subrogation right
The principle of indemnity
questions.explanation: Geographical trading restrictions are commonly expressed as warranties or conditions of cover.

questions.question: An insured vessel suffers repair costs of USD 2 million. The insured value and policy limit are sufficient, but the policy contains a USD 250,000 deductible. Ignoring other adjustments, which principle best explains why the insured should not receive more than the covered financial loss after the deductible?
options: Subrogation
Indemnity
Contribution
Utmost good faith
questions.explanation: Indemnity limits recovery to the actual covered loss and remains subject to the deductible and other policy terms.

questions.question: A shipowner receives full compensation from its insurer and later independently recovers the same loss from the negligent repair yard. Why may the insurer be entitled to the third-party recovery?
options: Because the insurer automatically becomes the owner of the vessel
Because subrogation prevents double recovery and transfers recovery rights after payment
Because contribution requires all third parties to share insured losses
Because utmost good faith requires the repair yard to pay the insurer directly
questions.explanation: Once the insurer has indemnified the insured, subrogation generally gives the insurer rights to recover from the responsible third party.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes contribution from subrogation?
options: Contribution concerns recovery from negligent third parties, while subrogation concerns multiple insurers
Contribution shares a loss among insurers, while subrogation allows recovery from a responsible third party
Contribution determines the cause of loss, while subrogation determines the insured value
Contribution applies before a policy is issued, while subrogation applies only when the premium is unpaid
questions.explanation: Contribution allocates liability among insurers covering the same risk, while subrogation concerns recovery from a third party responsible for the loss.

questions.question: A vessel grounds after the master deliberately deviates from the approved trading area to avoid congestion. The policy contains a clear geographical warranty. Which issue should be assessed separately from identifying the physical cause of the grounding?
options: Whether the insured complied with the policy warranty
Whether several insurers should contribute to the claim
Whether the insurer has already exercised subrogation
Whether the vessel's market value increased after the casualty
questions.explanation: The physical cause of the casualty and compliance with an express policy warranty are separate coverage issues.
